playbook:
When deciding my catch for the first season, I submit exactly the calculated sustainable share to signal cooperation and encourage a sustainable harvest.

When reviewing the previous season, I check the other boats' catches to see if they are overfishing or cooperating. 

If the other boats are also taking the sustainable share, I continue submitting the sustainable share to maximize long-term yield, until the final season.

If the other boats are overfishing, I do not incrementally increase my catch to match them; doing so only guarantees an early crash and a low total score for myself. 

When the stock is dropping rapidly due to overfishing and a crash becomes inevitable before the final season, I abandon sustainability and submit a catch request large enough to take the entire remaining stock, ensuring I capture the maximum possible share before it hits zero.

When playing the final season, I always submit a catch request for the entire remaining stock. Regeneration no longer matters, and doing so ensures I get an equal or larger split of the remaining pool if the other boats also defect at the end.

1.text:
When the first season begins, I submit exactly the sustainable share calculated by the harbour. I do not exceed it, as attempting to get ahead early immediately triggers a downward spiral and encourages other boats to overfish.

When reviewing the previous season's catches, if the other players took an amount similar to mine, I do not escalate my catch in the next season. I maintain the sustainable share to keep the stock stable and maximize the long-term yield.

When I see the stock dropping significantly, I reduce my catch to the new sustainable limit to signal cooperation and allow regeneration, rather than panicking and increasing my catch.

When the stock falls below the total amount the fleet caught in the previous season, or when it is the final season of the game, I submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock to secure my maximum possible share before the game ends or the fishery inevitably collapses.

I do not try to out-compete other players in the early or middle seasons. Escalating my catch just to keep pace with or beat the other boats does not work; it only accelerates the destruction of the fishery and lowers my final total score.

2.text:
When I start a new game, I submit exactly the sustainable share in the first season to establish a cooperative baseline and give the stock a chance to replenish.

In subsequent seasons, I evaluate the catches of the other boats. If they have taken the sustainable share or less, I continue to submit the sustainable share.

When the record shows that other boats are consistently overfishing and the stock is dropping significantly below its maximum, I do not increase my catch by just a few units to gain a slight edge. Taking slightly more than the sustainable share only guarantees a premature collapse where I am outcompeted. 

When it becomes clear that the stock is going to collapse because other players are defecting, I abandon sustainability entirely. 

When the remaining stock is low enough that the expected aggressive catches of the other boats will exceed it, or when it is the final season of the game, I submit a catch request equal to the entire remaining stock to maximize my proportional share of the final payout.
